# nish/json-pointer

RFC 6901 JSON Pointers: parsed into their tokens, escaped, resolved against a `JsonDocument`, and checked, with JSON Schema's relative JSON Pointer beside them.

```ts
import {
  JSON_POINTER_ERR_SYNTAX,
  JSON_POINTER_NONE,
  isJsonPointer,
  isRelativeJsonPointer,
  jsonPointerEscape,
  jsonPointerParse,
  jsonPointerResolve,
} from "nish/json-pointer";
```

```ts
import { jsonPointerParse, jsonPointerResolve, isRelativeJsonPointer } from "nish/json-pointer"

const doc = new JsonDocument(new JsonLimits())
const root = doc.parseText('{"a/b":[10,20],"~":true}')
jsonPointerParse("/a~1b/1")                 // ["a/b", "1"]
doc.i64(jsonPointerResolve(doc, root, "/a~1b/1"))   // 20
jsonPointerResolve(doc, root, "/a~1b/-")    // JSON_POINTER_NONE
jsonPointerResolve(doc, root, "a")          // JSON_POINTER_ERR_SYNTAX
isRelativeJsonPointer("1/a~1b")             // true
```

Whether `s` is a relative JSON Pointer: a non-negative integer with no leading zero (`0`, `12`, not `01`, `+1` or `-1`), then `#`, or an optional `+` or `-` and another such integer and then a JSON Pointer, which may be empty.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="json​Pointer​Resolve" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#jsonpointerresolve">

<scalar-detail title="The grammar">

A pointer is empty, naming the whole document, or a run
of `/`-led tokens, each any bytes but `/`, with `~0` for `~` and `~1` for
`/` and no other `~`. A token names an object's member by its key, bytes
for bytes, and an array's element by an index written `0` or without a
leading zero; `-`, the place after the last element, names nothing, as
does an index past the end, a token on a scalar, and a key not there. The
pointer is the decoded string, not a URI fragment: `#/a` is not one.

</scalar-detail>

A relative JSON Pointer (draft-bhutton-relative-json-pointer-00, which
JSON Schema 2020-12's `relative-json-pointer` format names) is a
non-negative integer written without a leading zero, then either `#`, or
an optional index manipulation (`+` or `-` and another such integer) and
a JSON Pointer: `0#`, `1/a`, `0+1/a`, `2-1`, not `0+1#`. Only its form is
checked here: resolving one needs the place it is relative to, which a
validator walking an instance holds.

<scalar-detail title="What a call costs">

`isJsonPointer` and `isRelativeJsonPointer` read
the text once and allocate nothing. `jsonPointerParse` allocates each
token and the array. `jsonPointerResolve` reads the pointer once and
allocates each token it decodes; a member is found by `JsonDocument.get`,
which steps through the object's members, so a step costs the object's
size.

</scalar-detail>

## Functions

### isJsonPointer

Whether `s` is an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer (the module header's grammar).
Allocates nothing.

```ts
function isJsonPointer(s: string): boolean
```

<scalar-field name="s" type="string" required>

the text to check.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="boolean">

true when `s` is a JSON Pointer, the empty one included.

</scalar-field>

### isRelativeJsonPointer

Whether `s` is a relative JSON Pointer: a non-negative integer with no
leading zero (`0`, `12`, not `01`, `+1` or `-1`), then `#`, or an optional
`+` or `-` and another such integer and then a JSON Pointer, which may be
empty. Allocates nothing.

```ts
function isRelativeJsonPointer(s: string): boolean
```

<scalar-field name="s" type="string" required>

the text to check.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="boolean">

true when `s` is a relative JSON Pointer.

</scalar-field>

### jsonPointerEscape

`token` written as one token of a JSON Pointer: `~` as `~0` and `/` as
`~1`, so `"a/b"` is `a~1b`. Everything else is copied whole.

```ts
function jsonPointerEscape(token: string): string
```

<scalar-field name="token" type="string" required>

one reference token, as it reads in an object key.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="string">

the token as it is written inside a pointer.

</scalar-field>

### jsonPointerParse

The reference tokens of JSON Pointer `p`, decoded: `[]` for `""`,
`["a/b", "", "~"]` for `/a~1b//~0`. `null` when `p` is not a JSON Pointer.

```ts
function jsonPointerParse(
  p: string,
): string[] | null
```

<scalar-field name="p" type="string" required>

the pointer text.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="string[] | null">

the decoded reference tokens, in order, or `null` when `p` is not a
  JSON Pointer.

</scalar-field>

### jsonPointerResolve

The value JSON Pointer `p` names in `root` of `doc`: `root` itself for
`""`, else each token taken in turn, as the module header says.
`JSON_POINTER_NONE` when the pointer names nothing there (or `root` names
no value), and `JSON_POINTER_ERR_SYNTAX` when `p` is not a JSON Pointer.

```ts
function jsonPointerResolve(
  doc: JsonDocument,
  root: i32,
  p: string,
): i32
```

<scalar-field name="doc" type="JsonDocument" required>

the document to look in.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="root" type="i32" required>

the value the pointer starts from.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="p" type="string" required>

the pointer text.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="i32">

the handle of the value named, `JSON_POINTER_NONE`, or
  `JSON_POINTER_ERR_SYNTAX`.

</scalar-field>
